content:
I couldn't find the GitHub scopes documented anywhere. The specification says only that the
server "reads permissions.push with that token before discarding it". In particular, read:org is requested on submission but it's not very clear why.

Would it be worth naming the scopes and their purpose on the submit page, or in
CONTRIBUTING? The rest of the protocol is really precise about what each step
publishes, so it seems incongruous to me.

(Really nice project, BTW)

Good catch. That permission is only needed to check if the submission is being made by a Palomar maintainer, which skips some checks (i.e. lets us do test submissions). But this information is available other ways (in particular, I can just hard code these identities!), and there's no need for asking all users for this.

So we won't!
